newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-ALBANIANS CALL ON SPANISH CLUBS TO SIGN THEM.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ALBANIANS CALL ON SPANISH CLUBS TO SIGN THEM.

text.p: Six Albanian under-21 international soccer players seeking political asylum in Spain pleaded on Tuesday with Spanish clubs to sign them.

The six, and the team masseur, sought asylum in April after the European soccer governing body UEFA had ordered their match against Germany to be played in the Spanish town of Guadix because of the unstable political situation in Albania.
Only one of the group, Ervin Fakaj, has been signed by a Spanish club, second division side Toledo.
"We realised it would be difficult to get signed by a first division club but we all thought that we'd be playing in the second division," said their spokesman Kresnik Zeka.

"The problem is that we do not have the knowledge of how to go about getting a contract and what to put on it. The Spanish federation promised to act as our agents but only Ervin has been found a team."
FIFA, the sport's world ruling body, has authorised the Spanish football federation to allow the signing of the players while they wait to see whether they are given refugee status.
They are presently learning to speak Spanish in the mornings and training in the afternoons.
